item.title: Homicide Mortality Among Female Adolescents and Women Aged 15 to 44 Years and US State Abortion Policies
item.description:
Importance: Homicide is a leading cause of death among female adolescents and women aged 15 to 44 years (hereinafter, women of reproductive age) in the US. Whether homicide trajectories differed across state abortion policy environments after the COVID-19 surge and the Dobbs v Jackson Women's Health Organization (hereinafter, Dobbs) decision is unclear.

Objectives: To characterize national homicide trends among women of reproductive age and assess whether post-2022 trajectories in homicide mortality among women of reproductive age diverged between states with and without sustained abortion bans.

Design, setting, and participants: This quasi-experimental study used national interrupted time series and comparative interrupted time series analyses of homicide mortality from January 1, 2016, through December 31, 2024, among women of reproductive age.

Exposure: The COVID-19 pandemic and sustained state abortion bans after Dobbs.

Main outcomes and measures: The main outcome was monthly homicide deaths. The population-offset Poisson model estimated differential post-Dobbs changes in homicide rates. Absolute rate differences, excess deaths, and years of life lost were estimated from fitted and counterfactual Poisson models. States with sustained total or near-total abortion bans after Dobbs were compared with states without such bans; states with partial or legally fluid restrictions were excluded. A triple-difference analysis comparing those aged 15 to 29 years with those aged 45 to 59 years served as a negative-control analysis.

Results: The analysis included 19 118 homicide deaths among women of reproductive age. Nationally, homicide increased sharply during the COVID-19 surge and subsequently decreased, with no clear national level or slope change beginning in July 2022. In policy-stratified analyses, however, homicide trajectories diverged. After July 2022, the exposed states (those with total or near-total abortion bans) vs unexposed states homicide monthly rate ratio (RR) was 1.006 (95% CI, 1.000-1.011; P = .03). Across calendar years 2023 and 2024, the fitted homicide rate in exposed states was higher than the modeled counterfactual (2023: RR, 1.07; 95% bootstrap interval, 1.01-1.13; and 2024: RR, 1.15; 95% bootstrap interval, 1.03-1.29). This corresponded to an estimated 48 excess deaths (95% bootstrap interval, 11-81) in 2023 and 87 excess deaths (95% bootstrap interval, 20-149) in 2024. A triple-difference model indicated greater post-Dobbs divergence among those aged 15 to 29 years than those aged 45 to 59 years (monthly ratio of RRs, 1.017; 95% CI, 1.000-1.034; P = .046); placebo Dobbs dates yielded nonsignificant results.

Conclusions and relevance: In this study, national homicide mortality rates among women of reproductive age returned toward prepandemic levels after COVID-19, but post-2022 trajectories diverged across state abortion policy environments. The findings suggest that national improvements in homicide mortality rates among women of reproductive age may mask less-favorable homicide trends among women of reproductive age in states with sustained abortion bans.

item.title: Clinical Decision Support for Fall Prevention in Primary Care: The eSTEPS Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults. Although exercise reduces fall risk, implementation in primary care remains limited.

Objective: To assess whether an electronic health record-integrated clinical decision support intervention, Electronic Strategies for Tailored Exercise to Prevent Falls (eSTEPS), reduces falls among older primary care patients at increased risk.

Design, setting, and participants: This matched-pair cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted from June 9, 2023, to May 8, 2025, with 12 to 23 months of follow-up at primary care practices within an integrated health system in the US. Adults aged 65 years or older with a positive 3-item fall-risk screen at a primary care visit were included.

Intervention: eSTEPS decision support embedded in the electronic health record with tailored exercise recommendations, optional physical therapy referral, and patient-facing materials (handouts, website, and app).

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the rate of patients with 1 or more falls identified using electronic health record-derived International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) diagnostic codes. Secondary outcomes were the rate of patients with 1 or more fall-related injuries identified by validated ICD-10 algorithms and mortality.

Results: Among 11 945 participants (mean [SD] age, 77.05 [7.43] years; 8044 females [67.3%]), of whom 5681 (47.6%) were in the intervention group and 6264 (52.4%) were in the control group, at 22 primary care practices, the rate of 1 or more ICD-10-coded falls (including falls with injuries) per 100 patient-years over the study period was 19.3 (95% CI, 18.6-20.1) in patients from intervention practices vs 21.2 (95% CI, 20.2-22.1) in patients from control practices (rate ratio [RR], 0.91 [95% CI, 0.88-0.95]; P < .001). The rate of ICD-10-coded fall-related injuries per 100 patient-years was 15.7 (95% CI, 15.0-16.5) from intervention practices vs 16.7 (95% CI, 16.1-17.4) from control practices over the study period (RR for fall injuries per 100 patient-years, 0.94 [95% CI, 0.90-0.97]; P = .001). No differences were observed in mortality. For intervention patients, eSTEPS exercise prescriptions were issued for 1255 patients (22.1%). Overall, 215 clinicians (77.9%) in intervention practices used the clinical decision support to deliver the exercise program at least once over the study period.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cluster randomized clinical trial of an electronic health record-integrated decision support, falls and fall-related injuries were modestly reduced in older adults in primary care. These results suggest support for scalable, workflow-integrated fall prevention.

item.title: Substance Misuse Prevalence and Risk Factors in Adolescents and Young Adults With Depression
item.description:
Importance: The prevalence of youths with mental health conditions has increased in recent years. Youths with mental health conditions are at risk of substance misuse via coping and self-regulation pathways; there is therefore a need to identify and address barriers to integrated mental health and substance use treatment in these youths.

Objective: To examine the prevalence of and motivations for prescription psychotherapeutic drug misuse among youths with and without depression.

Design, setting, and participants: A cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 and 2024 National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH) using a nationally representative survey of noninstitutionalized individuals aged 12 years and older related to drugs of misuse and mental health disorders. Data on adolescents and young adults were analyzed from January to March 2026.

Exposure: Past-year major depressive episode (MDE).

Main outcomes and measure: The primary outcome was past-year prescription psychotherapeutic drug misuse and use disorder, and the secondary outcome was motivations for misuse. Survey-weighted prevalence estimates with 95% CIs were calculated and group differences were assessed using χ2 tests. To assess the association between drug misuse and depression, logistic regression models were used.

Results: The 2023 and 2024 NSDUH included 22 906 adolescents (aged 12-17 years) and 27 723 young adults (aged 18-25 years), among whom 24 831 (49.1%) were males, 13 256 (26.2%) were Hispanic, 6923 (13.7%) were non-Hispanic Black, 23 114 (45.6%) were non-Hispanic White, and 7336 (14.5%) were non-Hispanic-all other races. A past-year MDE was reported by 16.3% (95% CI, 15.6%-17.0%) of respondents, corresponding to an estimated 9.8 million individuals nationally. Among youths with a past-year MDE, 6.6% (95% CI, 5.8%-7.5%) reported misuse of psychotherapeutic drugs while 6.0% (95% CI, 5.2%-6.9%) reported use disorder. Youths with a past-year MDE had significantly higher odds of reporting prescription drug misuse (odds ratio [OR], 2.09; 95% CI, 1.75-2.50) and prescription drug use disorder (OR, 4.02; 95% CI, 3.37-4.80) compared with those without a past-year MDE. Compared with youths without a past-year MDE, youths with a past-year MDE were more likely to report misusing opioid analgesics (10.2% [95% CI, 6.4%-15.9%] vs 3.7% [95% CI, 2.2%-6.3%]; P = .01) and tranquilizers (29.8% [95% CI, 21.1%-40.3%] vs 13.2% [95% CI, 5.8%-19.9%]; P = .003) to help with feelings and emotions.

Conclusions and relevance: This cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 and 2024 NSDUH found that youths with depression were more likely than their peers without depression both to report prescription drug misuse and to meet criteria for prescription drug use disorder. For certain medications, this misuse was more often motivated by a desire to address feelings and emotions. These findings underscore the need to identify and address barriers to integrated mental health and substance use treatment for at-risk youths before patterns of self-medication progress to enduring substance use disorders.

item.title: Preterm Risk Factors, Epigenetic Age, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes
item.description:
Importance: Studies examining biological factors associated with neurodevelopment in the preterm population are limited. It was previously demonstrated that epigenetic age acceleration was associated with better neurodevelopmental outcomes among children born preterm. It is unclear whether this association is modified by clinical and environmental preterm risk factors.

Objective: To examine whether the association between epigenetic aging and neurodevelopmental outcomes is modified by preterm brain injury and socioeconomic status.

Design, setting, and participants: This was a prospective cohort study of children born at 24 to 32 weeks' gestation, recruited from 2 neonatal intensive care units from 2015 to 2019 and followed up to January 2026. The cohort was well characterized with clinical data, brain magnetic resonance imaging, and neurodevelopmental assessments (Bayley-III cognitive and motor domains) at 3 years. Participants with buccal epithelial cell DNA collected at 3 years were included.

Exposure: Epigenetic age (in weeks) at 3 years was determined using the pediatric buccal epigenetic clock and corrected for chronological age to give epigenetic age difference.

Main outcomes and measures: Primary analyses used linear regression to examine the association between epigenetic age difference, preterm risk factors (any brain injury, severe brain injury, maternal educational level), and cognitive and motor outcomes at 3 years. Secondary analyses examined whether brain injury and maternal education level modified the associations between epigenetic age difference and cognitive and motor outcomes at 3 years.

Results: A total of 102 study participants (median gestational age, 27.0 weeks [IQR, 25.6-28.9 weeks]; 54 female [53%]) were included. Higher maternal educational level (β = 11.65; 95% CI, 3.55-19.76; P = .005) and epigenetic age acceleration (β = 0.07; 95% CI, 0.01-0.14; P = .04) were associated with higher cognitive scores. Epigenetic age acceleration was also associated with higher motor scores (β = 0.16; 95% CI, 0.06-0.27; P = .003), while extreme prematurity (β = -5.66; 95% CI, -10.85 to -0.46; P = .03) and severe brain injury (β = -10.99; 95% CI, -21.32 to -0.66; P = .04) were associated with lower motor scores. Severe brain injury modified the association between epigenetic aging and motor outcomes (β = 0.41; 95% CI, 0.08-0.74; P = .02), and children with epigenetic age acceleration in the presence of severe brain injury had higher motor scores.

Conclusions and relevance: In this prospective preterm cohort study, epigenetic aging, severe brain injury, and socioeconomic status were associated with neurodevelopmental outcomes. Children with severe brain injury along with epigenetic age acceleration had higher motor scores. These findings suggest the association between epigenetic aging and neurodevelopment is context dependent and can vary based on the presence of preterm risk factors.

item.title: Cervical Cancer Screening Rates by Race and Ethnicity, Age, Language, and Census Region
item.description:
Importance: Longitudinal evidence of cervical cancer screening (CCS) trends before and after COVID-19 across demographic cohorts remains limited.

Objective: To examine CCS rates by race and ethnicity, age, language, and census region among patients with at least 1 health care encounter in an electronic medical record (EMR) system from 2019 through 2024, and to evaluate longitudinal trends across these groups.

Design, setting, and participants: Using an EMR database, this cross-sectional study evaluated CCS rates among female patients aged 21 to 64 years between 2019 and 2024, stratified by race and ethnicity, age, language, and census region.

Exposures: Race and ethnicity, age, language, and census region.

Main outcomes and measures: Descriptive statistics were used to summarize annual CCS rates across demographic groups. The Cochran-Armitage test assessed linear trends over time.

Results: Annual sample sizes ranged from approximately 9 to 16 million patients and increased steadily over time; analytic population sizes varied across subgroups. Most patients were non-Hispanic White, aged 30 to 49 years, English-speaking, and resided in either the South or Northeast. Non-Hispanic White patients had the highest annual CCS rates from 2019 to 2021 but experienced the smallest percentage increase, from 10.98% (95% CI, 10.96%-11.01%) to 13.85% (95% CI, 13.82%-13.87%), over the study period. Hispanic patients experienced the largest percentage increase in CCS rates, from 9.85% (95% CI, 9.80%-9.90%) to 15.51% (95% CI, 15.47%-15.55%). American Indian, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander patients had the lowest screening rates throughout the study period. Patients aged 30 to 49 years and non-English-speaking patients consistently had the highest CCS rates across all years. Patients in the Western and Southern census regions had lower CCS rates than those in other regions.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study of patients with at least 1 health care encounter in an EMR system, all CCS rates increased across all racial and ethnic groups from 2019 to 2024, with the greatest gains observed among Hispanic patients. However, persistent disparities remained, particularly among American Indian, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander patients and those in the Western and Southern regions. These findings suggest that although screening uptake has improved over time, substantial geographic and racial and ethnic disparities in CCS persist, highlighting important areas for future research and intervention efforts.

item.title: Laser Therapy for Sexual Health in Breast Cancer Survivors Receiving Aromatase Inhibitors: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Laser therapy is increasingly used to treat genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) in breast cancer survivors, but sham-controlled evidence of benefit remains limited.

Objective: To evaluate 12-month efficacy and safety of fractional carbon dioxide (CO2) laser therapy (CLT) vs sham laser therapy (SLT) for GSM in breast cancer survivors receiving aromatase inhibitors.

Design, setting, and participants: This is a secondary analysis of a single-center, double-blind, sham-controlled randomized clinical trial conducted at a tertiary academic hospital in Spain. Participants included breast cancer survivors with GSM and dyspareunia receiving aromatase inhibitors, recruited from October 30, 2020, to September 1, 2021. Participants were followed up for 12 months. Data were analyzed from December 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025.

Intervention: Five monthly sessions of CLT or SLT plus first-line nonhormonal therapy (FLT), including vaginal moisturizers and vibrators.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) score. Secondary outcomes included rate of sexual activity, dyspareunia, Spanish Body Image Scale, quality of life (12-Item Short Form Health Survey), Vaginal Health Index, objective parameters (pH, vaginal maturation index, epithelial measures), serum estradiol level, FLT adherence, and adverse events.

Results: Of the 84 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 53.8 [8.8] years), 67 completed the 12-month follow-up (CLT, 32; SLT, 35). The CLT group did not differ from the SLT group in FSFI score change from baseline to 12 months (difference, CLT vs SLT, -0.69 [95% CI, -3.58 to 2.20]; P = .64), nor in any secondary outcome. Across the full sample, significant improvements from baseline to 12 months were observed in FSFI score (18.9 to 23.0; mean difference, 4.5 [95% CI, 3.1-5.9]; P < .001), dyspareunia (mean difference, -3.7 [95% CI, -4.4 to -3.0]; P < .001), Spanish Body Image Scale (mean difference, -3.9 [95% CI, -5.1 to -2.8]; P < .001), and Vaginal Health Index (mean difference, 4.2 [95% CI, 3.1-5.2]; P < .001). Sexual activity increased among 57 of 67 participants (85.1%; odds ratio, 2.35 [95% CI, 1.23-4.50]; P = .009). Improvements were found in pH (mean difference, -0.5 [95% CI, -0.8 to -0.2]; P < .001) and vaginal maturation index (mean difference, 19.0% [95% CI, 13.4%-24.5%]; P < .001). FLT adherence was similar between groups. No severe adverse effects occurred.

Conclusions and relevance: In this randomized clinical trial of breast cancer survivors receiving aromatase inhibitors, vulvovaginal CLT provided no additional benefit for sexual or vaginal health at 12 months. Improvements in both groups likely reflected FLT adherence, trial participation, or contextual factors rather than laser efficacy. High-quality sham-controlled trials remain essential before routine implementation.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04619485.

item.title: Organ Preservation and Quality of Life After Total Neoadjuvant Treatment in Rectal Cancer
item.description:
Importance: Data on quality of life (QOL) after total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) are important for counseling patients on the benefits of watch-and-wait (WW) vs total mesorectal excision (TME) for rectal cancer. A thorough understanding of both options and their long-term impact on bowel, urinary, sexual function, and other QOL domains remains limited.

Objective: To examine the association of organ preservation with QOL and functional outcomes among patients with rectal cancer treated in 2 phase 2 clinical trials.

Design, setting, and participants: This unplanned, post hoc, cohort study used data from the CAO/ARO/AIO-12 and CAO/ARO/AIO-16 trials, recruiting participants from June 15, 2015, through October 7, 2020, from 19 centers in Germany. Included patients had cT3 to cT4 or node-positive rectal adenocarcinoma. Total neoadjuvant treatment included chemoradiation therapy combined with induction or consolidation chemotherapy. The statistical analysis was performed from March 6 to December 23, 2025.

Main outcomes and measures: The association of WW with functional outcomes and QOL was assessed using prospectively recorded EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-CR29, and Wexner score questionnaires. Differences in QOL scores were estimated using adjusted longitudinal and cross-sectional analyses with a predefined clinically meaningful difference of at least 5 points.

Results: Baseline questionnaires were available from 346 of 385 eligible patients (89.9%; median [range] age, 60 [19-80] years; 257 male [67%]), while available QOL questionnaires decreased over time to 185 (48.1%) at 5 years. Using the longitudinal analytic approach, statistically significant and clinically meaningful differences in favor of WW were noted for fecal incontinence (-21.2 [95% CI, -30.0 to -12.3]; P < .001); stool frequency (-19.8 [95% CI, -27.6 to -11.9]; P < .001); embarrassment (-17.0 [95% CI, -27.4 to -6.6]; P = .002); flatulence (-15.2 [95% CI, -24.4 to -6.0]; P < .001), buttock pain (-11.9 [95% CI, -20.8 to -3.0]; P = .01); social (9.7 [95% CI, 1.1-18.3]; P = .03), physical (10.2 [95% CI, 4.1-16.3]; P = .002), and role (13.9 [95% CI, 4.9-22.9]; P = .003) functioning; and global health status (9.2 [95% CI, 3.2-15.2]; P = .004). These clinically meaningful differences were detectable in both the intended organ preservation and disease-free groups. Patients with sustained clinical complete response at 3 years (n = 29) vs those with pathologic complete response or matched baseline characteristics favored WW for fecal incontinence (-24.0 and -11.6, respectively), stool frequency (-34.6 and -19.1), sore skin (-18.0 and -18.1), buttock pain (-14.7 and -17.6), embarrassment (-41.1 and -20.5), role functioning (19.1 and 10.9), and social functioning (20.0 and 8.4).

Conclusions and relevance: In the absence of prospective randomized trials, this study provides evidence suggesting long-term clinically meaningful benefits for organ preservation regarding QOL, especially for most gastrointestinal subscales, social functioning, and global health status, over a 5-year period among patients with rectal cancer. As treatment options for patients with rectal cancer now routinely include WW in cases of clinical complete response after TNT, patient-reported QOL measures have become paramount for informed shared decision-making.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT02363374 and NCT03561142.

item.title: Socioeconomic Inequality and Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events
item.description:
Importance: Low socioeconomic status is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease, yet it remains unclear whether this association has changed over time. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) are key contributors to cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, and health care costs and, thus, are indicators of the overall cardiovascular burden.

Objective: To describe temporal trends in incident MACE by equivalized income groups in the Danish population from 1988 to 2023.

Design, setting, and participants: This nationwide, population-based open cohort study using data from Danish national registries included all residents of Denmark aged 30 years or older who were alive in each year between January 1, 1988, and January 1, 2023, and had available income observations in the current or preceding 5 years. Individuals were followed up to December 31 of each year, to death, or to emigration. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to July 2026.

Exposure: Equivalized disposable household income.

Main outcome and measures: Incident MACE, defined as the first hospital admission for acute myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke, or heart failure. Age-standardized incidence rates were calculated annually, stratified by income quartile and sex.

Results: A total of 5 932 672 individuals aged 30 years or older were registered in the Danish Civil Registration System from 1988 to 2023. The annual study population increased from 3.06 million in 1988 to 3.85 million in 2023. Most residents in 1988 were female (52.1%), and most in 2023 were male (51.1%); the median age increased from 50.8 years (IQR, 40.2-65.6 years) in 1988 to 55.8 years (IQR, 43.3-68.8 years) in 2023. Age-standardized incidence rates of MACE decreased across all income groups from 1988 to 2023 but remained highest in the lowest income quartile. For males, the rate decreased from 191.1 (95% CI, 186.3-196.0) per 10 000 person-years to 119.6 (95% CI, 116.0-123.2) per 10 000 person-years in the lowest income quartile, while in the highest quartile it decreased from 153.5 (95% CI, 142.9-164.0) per 10 000 person-years to 85.9 (95% CI, 81.2-90.6) per 10 000 person-years. For females, the rate decreased from 116.0 (95% CI, 113.0-118.9) per 10 000 person-years to 70.4 (95% CI, 68.1-72.6) per 10 000 person-years in in the lowest income quartile and from 89.5 (95% CI, 81.9-97.2) per 10 000 person-years to 53.1 (95% CI, 49.0-57.1) per 10 000 person-years in the highest.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of Danish residents aged 30 years or older from 1988 to 2023, the incidence of MACE declined across all socioeconomic groups. Although individuals with lower income generally experienced higher incidence rates, the overall decline occurred in all socioeconomic groups.

item.title: Ultraprocessed Food Intake and Adiposity, Vascular Brain Injury, and Cognition in Middle-Aged Adults
item.description:
Importance: Ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) account for a substantial and increasing proportion of dietary intake in Canada. Although UPFs are consistently associated with adiposity and cardiometabolic disease, their associations with subclinical vascular brain injury (VBI) and cognitive performance in midlife are unclear.

Objective: To evaluate associations of UPF consumption with adiposity, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined VBI, and cognitive performance in middle-aged adults in Canada.

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional study included 8783 adults aged 35 to 69 years without cardiovascular disease who were enrolled in the Canadian Alliance for Healthy Hearts and Healthy Minds (CAHHM) and Prospective Urban and Rural Epidemiology-MIND (PURE-MIND) studies. Participants from CAHHM were recruited from January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2018, and participants from PURE-MIND were recruited from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2018. Data analyses were conducted between July 16, 2024, and August 16, 2026.

Exposures: UPF consumption assessed using previously validated semiquantitative food frequency questionnaires and expressed as servings per 2000 kcal/d.

Main outcomes and measures: The main outcomes were body fat (BF) percentage (bioelectrical impedance), visceral adipose tissue (VAT) volume, hepatic fat fraction (HFF), VBI defined as covert brain infarcts or high white matter hyperintensities (HWMHs) (measured by MRI), and cognitive performance measured by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) and the Digital Symbol Substitution Test (DSST).

Results: In this cross-sectional study of 8783 participants (mean [SD] age, 57.7 [8.7] years; 4917 females [56.6%]), those in the highest quartile of UPF intake had a BF percentage that was 1.7 (95% CI, 1.2-2.2) percentage points higher and a 5.7 (95% CI, 3.2-8.3) mL greater VAT volume compared with those in the lowest quartile, but no significant difference in HFF. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest UPF quartile had higher odds of VBI (adjusted OR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.10-1.77; P for trend = .009). No significant associations were observed between UPF intake and MOCA or DSST performance.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study of middle-aged adults in Canada, higher UPF intake was associated with greater adiposity and higher odds of MRI-defined VBI but not cognitive performance. Associations with VBI were sensitive to UPF exposure definition. Longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporality.

item.title: Survival Outcomes With Lu-177 PSMA by Treatment Line and Taxane Sequencing in Prostate Cancer
item.description:
Importance: Lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Lu-177) prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a targeted radioligand therapy approved for patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant (mAPMR) prostate cancer after progression on androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs). Data to guide treatment sequencing are limited.

Objective: To evaluate survival outcomes in patients with mAPMR prostate cancer receiving Lu-177 PSMA by line of therapy and the timing of taxane exposure.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study used a deidentified electronic health record research database to obtain comprehensive longitudinal oncology data from community and academic practices across the US. Among patients with metastatic prostate cancer in the dataset, those who received Lu-177 PSMA after an ARPI between December 19, 2018, and June 23, 2025, met the inclusion criteria. The data cutoff was June 30, 2025.

Exposure: Receipt of Lu-177 PSMA, stratified by line of therapy and timing of taxane exposure (before Lu-177 PSMA, after Lu-177 PSMA, or never received taxane).

Main outcomes and measures: Primary end points were clinical time to next treatment (TTNT; defined as the time from Lu-177 PSMA initiation to next systemic therapy or death) and clinical overall survival (OS; defined as the time from Lu-177 PSMA initiation to death). Both outcomes were censored at last follow-up and estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method with 95% CIs.

Results: Among the 850 patients included, the median (IQR) age was 74 (68-80) years; most were treated in community settings (598 [70.4%]) and had commercial insurance (520 [61.2%]). A total of 466 patients (54.8%) received taxane before Lu-177 PSMA, 35 (4.1%) received taxane after Lu-177 PSMA, and 349 (41.1%) never received taxane. Median clinical TTNT and clinical OS with Lu-177 PSMA were 8.0 (95% CI, 7.4-9.0) months and 12.0 (95% CI, 11.0-13.0) months for patients with taxane exposure before Lu-177 PSMA; 10.0 (95% CI, 9.2-11.0) months and 14.0 (95% CI, 13.0-17.0) months for patients who never received taxane; and 6.0 (95% CI, 4.9-8.0) months and 16.0 (95% CI, 13.0-not reached) months for patients with taxane exposure after Lu-177 PSMA, respectively.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study, outcomes with Lu-177 PSMA were broadly consistent across treatment lines and taxane sequencing groups. These findings may help inform patient counseling, although prospective studies are needed to determine the optimal treatment sequencing strategy.

item.title: Disparities in α1-Antitrypsin Deficiency Testing and Treatment in US Adults
item.description:
Importance: α1-Antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is underdiagnosed despite guidelines for broad testing, and the factors associated with low testing and treatment are not well known.

Objective: To identify factors associated with low AATD testing and augmentation therapy in individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma.

Design, setting, and participants: This is a retrospective, multicenter cohort study using national electronic health record data from the Veterans Health Administration from January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2024. Data analysis was conducted from July to October 2025. Participants were individuals with a diagnosis of COPD and/or asthma (≥2 International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision, or International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision codes).

Exposure: Individual demographics, comorbidities, tobacco use, rural-urban residence, Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), and drive time to the specialty care facility.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcomes were prevalence of and factors associated with AATD testing and augmentation therapy prescription. Multivariable regression models were used, adjusting sequentially for demographics, comorbidities, tobacco use, rural-urban residence, SVI, and drive time to the specialty care facility.

Results: Among 2 384 913 individuals with COPD and/or asthma (mean [SD] age, 64.2 [14.3] years; 178 898 female [7.5%]; 16 778 [0.7%] American Indian or Alaska Native; 14 996 [0.7%] Asian; 331 202 Black or African American [15.3%]; 19 029 [0.9%] Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander; 1 787 951 White [82.4%]), 138 278 (5.8%) underwent testing. In fully adjusted models, cirrhosis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.40; 95% CI, 6.29-6.51) and bronchiectasis (aOR, 3.73; 95% CI, 3.59-3.87) were associated with higher odds of testing. Older ages and active tobacco use were associated with lower odds of testing. Rural-urban residence and SVI had similar odds across categories. Longer drive times were associated with progressively lower odds of testing (>90 vs ≤30 minutes; aOR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.62-0.65). Of 8564 with AATD diagnosis, 320 (3.7%) were prescribed augmentation therapy and showed a similar pattern as testing, occurring less often among patients from minoritized racial and ethnic groups, those actively using tobacco, and those with longer drive times to specialty care, and more often among those with cirrhosis and bronchiectasis.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of individuals with COPD and/or asthma, AATD testing and augmentation therapy were profoundly low. System-level reform is needed to bridge gaps across age, comorbidities, tobacco use, and health care access.

item.title: Prehospital Point-of-Care GFAP for Detection of Intracranial Hemorrhage in Acute Nontraumatic Coma
item.description:
Importance: Rapid identification of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with acute nontraumatic coma is critical to guiding triage and early management; however, prehospital diagnostic tools remain limited.

Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of prehospital whole-blood point-of-care measurement of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) for detecting ICH.

Design, setting, and participants: This diagnostic study used data collected by a UK physician-paramedic helicopter emergency medical service between January 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. A consecutive sample of adult patients (aged ≥16 years) presenting with acute nontraumatic coma, defined as Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 12 or less, who underwent prehospital rapid sequence induction (RSI) of anesthesia with clinical suspicion of ICH were eligible for inclusion. Patients with traumatic pathology and those without follow-up data were excluded. Patients were observed for up for 30 days from hospital admission. Data analysis was performed in June 2026.

Exposure: Prehospital whole-blood point-of-care brain biomarker (GFAP and UCH-L1) testing using the i-STAT Alinity Point-of-Care Blood Analyzer (Abbott Laboratories).

Main outcome and measures: Diagnostic accuracy of GFAP and UCH-L1 for detecting ICH, using computed tomography as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive value, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated.

Results: The primary study cohort comprised 65 patients who underwent prehospital brain biomarker testing (median age, 63 [IQR, 47-69] years; 55.4% male). The median (IQR) GCS score was 4 (3-6). ICH was present in 50.8% (n = 33). Thirteen (20.0%) patients underwent neurosurgery, and the 30-day survival rate was 46.2% (n = 30). GFAP demonstrated high sensitivity (97.0%; 95% CI, 84.2%-99.9%) and discriminatory ability (AUC, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.87-0.99). UCH-L1 showed lower sensitivity (78.8%; 95% CI, 61.1%-91.0%) and specificity (18.8%; 95% CI, 7.2%-36.4%), with limited discriminatory performance. A combined biomarker approach achieved 100.0% sensitivity (95% CI, 89.4%-100.0%) and a negative predictive value of 100.0% (95% CI, 47.8%-100.0%).

Conclusions and relevance: In this diagnostic study of adults with acute nontraumatic coma undergoing prehospital RSI, point-of-care prehospital GFAP testing was feasible and demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy in detecting intracranial hemorrhage. Further prospective external validation is required to determine its association with triage, treatment decisions, and patient outcomes.

item.title: Direct Certification With Medicaid and School Lunch Participation Among Maryland Public Schools
item.description:
Importance: States may join the US Department of Agriculture Direct Certification with Medicaid (DCM) program, allowing schools to use Medicaid participation to automatically qualify students for free and reduced-price school meals (F/RP). DCM also informs the Identified Student Percentage (ISP), which determines eligibility for the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP). Pre-COVID-19 evaluations found mixed associations between DCM and school meal participation. Pandemic-era policies included free meals for all students, which has ended in most states. Therefore, a postpandemic evaluation of DCM is warranted.

Objective: To examine the association of Maryland's DCM implementation in the 2022-2023 school year (SY22-23) with ISP, CEP eligibility and enrollment, and school lunch participation.

Design, setting, and participants: In this cohort study, publicly available school-level data were used to examine annual ISP, CEP participation, and school lunch participation among public schools in Maryland. A school-level fixed effects model evaluated changes in school lunch participation before (SY18-19 and SY19-20) and after (SY22-23 and SY23-24) DCM implementation among non-CEP schools. A 2-way fixed effects model tested the association between CEP enrollment and school lunch participation among schools newly eligible for CEP due to DCM. Data analyses were conducted from July to December 2025.

Exposure: DCM implementation.

Main outcomes and measures: ISP, CEP eligibility and enrollment, and school lunch participation.

Results: Among 1252 schools, 856 (68.4%) were elementary, 221 (17.7%) were middle, and 175 (14.0%) were high schools; 734 (58.6%) were suburban, 258 (20.6%) were located in rural or small towns, and 260 (20.8%) were urban. Mean (SD) ISP increased from 25.9% (17.5%) in SY21-22 to 37.3% (19.6%) in SY22-23 after DCM implementation. In SY23-24, CEP eligibility and enrollment increased by 26.7 and 22.2 percentage points, respectively. School lunch participation increased by 1.9 (95% CI, 1.1-2.8) percentage points (P < .001) among non-CEP schools post-DCM (SY22-23 and SY23-24). Among schools newly participating in CEP, school lunch participation increased by 6.5 (95% CI, 4.6-8.3) percentage points (P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of Maryland public schools, DCM implementation was associated with increases in direct certification for F/RP meals, CEP participation, and lunch participation. DCM implementation may support school meal participation in the post-COVID-19 pandemic context. Programs such as CEP and Medicaid may warrant policy attention to support school meal access and its benefits for student health and academic outcomes.

item.title: Leadership Behavior, Values Alignment, and Future Objective Turnover Among Physicians
item.description:
Importance: Although US health care organizations are attempting to improve physician retention, national data indicate that physician turnover is increasing. There are minimal data on the associations between physicians' assessment of their immediate supervisor and alignment of individual and organizational values and objective turnover.

Objective: To evaluate the association between individual responses from physician surveys evaluating named immediate supervisor and alignment of individual and organizational values with objective turnover during the following 2 years.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study included practicing physicians completing organizational surveys at a large, academic medical center between October 3, 2016, and May 1, 2024. Standardized instruments were used to assess leader behavior, alignment of individual and organizational values, burnout, and professional fulfillment at 5 survey time points. Individual survey responses were paired with human resources records on objective turnover.

Exposure: The 9-item Mayo Clinic Leadership Impact Index, Stanford Values Alignment Scale, Stanford Professional Fulfillment Index, and a measure of self-reported intent to leave within the next 2 years were administered.

Main outcomes and measures: Objective turnover was determined from human resource records. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to evaluate the association of leader behavior and alignment of individual and organizational values with turnover, adjusting for age, sex, survey year, and occupational well-being measures associated with turnover (ie, burnout and professional fulfillment).

Results: In aggregate, 7351 survey responses from 3124 unique physicians (1528 [48.9%] female) paired with 2-year objective turnover were available. The participation rate exceeded 50% in all survey years (2016: 1281 of 2392 [53.6%]; 2019: 1285 of 1924 [66.8%]; 2020: 1479 of 1909 [77.5%]; 2022: 1553 of 2251 [69.0%]; 2024: 1654 of 2498 [66.2%]) Each 1-point higher score (range, 0-10) for leader behavior (hazard ratio [HR], 0.89 [95% CI, 0.85-0.93]; P < .001) and values alignment (HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.86-0.94]; P < .001) was associated with decreased objective 2-year turnover. After adjusting for age, sex, survey year, values alignment, occupational burnout, and professional fulfillment, each 1-point difference in leadership behavior score (HR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.83-0.94]; P < .001) remained associated with objective 2-year turnover. The association between values alignment and 2-year objective turnover was no longer present in these analyses. On paired individual-level data from physicians completing consecutive surveys and adjusting for baseline score, each 1-point increase in leader behavior (HR, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.76-0.90]; P < .001) and values alignment (HR, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.79-0.93]; P < .001) score between surveys was associated with reduced turnover following the second survey. On multivariable analysis adjusting for age, sex, and survey year, respondents indicating moderate (HR, 3.22 [95% CI, 2.41-4.31]) or likely to definite intent to leave (HR, 8.58 [95% CI, 6.43-11.44]; P < .001) were at higher risk of objective 2-year turnover.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study, physician evaluation of immediate supervisor behavior and alignment between individual and organizational values on organizational surveys were associated with subsequent objective turnover. These findings suggest that organizations seeking to promote physician retention should conduct leadership assessments, attend to leadership development, and foster values alignment with their physicians.

item.title: Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity Data and HIV Preexposure Prophylaxis Disparity Detection
item.description:
Importance: US federal reporting changes in 2025 removed sexual orientation and gender identity (SOGI) measures from health-center reporting, raising concerns about equity surveillance.

Objective: To quantify how incomplete or absent SOGI data are associated with detection of disparities in documented HIV preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) orders.

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional study used electronic health record data from a large safety-net health system in Southern California. Data were from patients 18 years or older registered as of October 28, 2025, with documented PrEP orders from January 2, 2019, through October 27, 2025. Registration dates were unavailable, precluding common follow-up. Three surveillance scenarios were assessed: complete SOGI, sex assigned at birth (SAAB) only, and joint SOGI missingness from 0% to 90%. Adults with classifiable SAAB, sexual orientation, and gender identity were included.

Exposures: Complete, unavailable, or partially missing SOGI data.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was any documented PrEP order. Logistic regression models adjusted for age and race and ethnicity, with interactions of sexual orientation or gender identity with SAAB. Marginally standardized probabilities and adjusted percentage-point differences were estimated within SAAB strata. Each nonzero missing level included 250 simulations to assess the magnitude, precision, and statistical detectability of each difference.

Results: This study included 165 198 adults (mean [SD] age, 45.0 [16.4] years). Most patients (97 621 [59.1%]) were female SAAB; 5790 (3.5%) were lesbian, gay, bisexual, or another sexual minority (LGB+) and 303 (0.2%) were transgender or gender diverse (TGD). A total of 1406 patients (0.9%) had a documented PrEP order. Under the complete SOGI analytic scenario, the adjusted probability of a documented PrEP order among cisgender patients assigned male at birth was 26.7 percentage points (pp) (95% CI, 24.9-28.5 pp; P < .001) higher for LGB+ patients than for heterosexual patients. Among all patients assigned male at birth, the adjusted probability was 12.3 pp (95% CI, 7.0-17.6 pp; P < .001) higher for TGD patients than for cisgender patients. Neither difference was significant among patients assigned female at birth. Under SAAB-only surveillance, only a difference between male and female SAAB was measurable (1.4 pp; 95% CI, 1.3-1.5 pp; P < .001), whereas SOGI-specific differences were not estimable. Under joint missing-completely-at-random deletion, positive-direction detectability of the male-SAAB sexual orientation difference remained at 100% through 90% missingness; detectability of the gender identity difference declined from 100% at 40% missingness to 51.6% at 80% missingness and 19.2% at 90% missingness. Selective missingness attenuated estimates.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study, the complete SOGI analytic scenario enabled estimation of SOGI-stratified differences, whereas SAAB-only surveillance did not. Partial collection preserved estimability but reduced precision, and selective missingness attenuated estimates.

item.title: Multi-Institutional Data for Faculty Well-Being Improvements Within and Across Medical Schools
item.description:
Importance: Burnout, engagement, and satisfaction vary in prevalence and correlate with organizational performance in US medical colleges. Large-scale improvements have been elusive.

Objective: To quantify rates of well-being and its organizational correlates so to help identify opportunities for shared learning and focus well-being interventions across and within medical schools.

Design, setting, and participants: In this cross-sectional study, 28 US medical schools accredited by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education were surveyed from January 26, 2021, through June 3, 2024. Of 28 919 eligible faculty, 16 994 participated (58.8%; range, 21% to 92%).

Exposure: The Association of American Medical Colleges' StandPoint Faculty Engagement Survey.

Main outcomes and measures: The psychological states of burnout, satisfaction, and organizational commitment as a proxy for engagement and their antecedents. Heterogeneity beyond chance was quantified in the rates across and within schools using the I2 statistic. Positive deviants, or bright spots, were identified as those schools and departments whose confidence intervals did not include the group mean rate. Regression analyses assessed the factors contributing to the success of the positive deviants.

Results: Across 15 404 respondents (9093 [53.5%] identified as men), a pooled 32% reported burnout. Across schools, there was substantial heterogeneity in rates beyond chance of burnout (13%-41%; I2 = 75%), commitment (pooled 80% [range, 74%-95%]; I2 = 82%), and satisfaction (pooled 77% [range, 62%-86%]; I2 = 80%). Few departments (67 of 502 [13.3%]) had a favorable rate of both commitment and burnout. For rates of burnout at the department level, 32% of the variance was explained by the rates of burnout of their school and discipline; the rates of autonomy, purpose, and belonging; and gender and age. The burnout of individuals was explained by the mean burnout score of one's department (R2 = 4%), with no contribution by the school or discipline. When combined with the factors contributing to departmental variation, 24% of the variance in burnout across individuals was explained.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study, the substantial heterogeneity beyond chance and identification of positive deviants (bright spots) support the opportunity for learning health systems and learning communities across and within schools and professional societies to identify positive deviant departments or schools and share details of implementing existing successful practices for promoting well-being. Both burnout and engagement should be monitored within and across medical schools, as these measures may not converge.

item.title: Cultural Engagement and Hospital-Treated Mental Disorders in Older Adults
item.description:
Importance: Cultural engagement is associated longitudinally with better mental health and reduced depression incidence, but evidence has largely relied on self-reported symptoms and diagnoses, leaving uncertainty about clinically recorded disorders, and residual confounding remains a concern.

Objective: To examine whether cultural engagement is associated with incident hospital-treated mental disorders.

Design, setting, and participants: This prospective cohort study included adults aged 50 years and older from the English Longitudinal Study of Aging (wave 4, May 2008 to July 2009), with follow-up through March 2024. Data were analyzed from November 2025 to March 2026.

Exposures: Frequency of engagement with any of the receptive arts activities (ie, watching or consuming performances or exhibitions) was categorized as never, infrequent (less than once a year up to once or twice a year), or frequent (every few months up to monthly or more).

Main outcomes and measures: Participant records were linked to diagnostic codes in Hospital Episode Statistics and mortality records with follow-up of up to 20 years. The primary outcomes were mental disorders overall and 4 main mental disorders (dementia, substance misuse, mood disorders, and neurotic disorders). Cox proportional hazard regression models were used to estimate the hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs, with a false discovery rate (FDR) approach for significance. To further probe causality, eye disease, ear disease, and traumatic brain injury-which share similar sociodemographic profiles to mental disorders-were prespecified as negative control outcomes.

Results: This study included 8274 adults (mean [SD] age, 65.4 [9.6] years; 4672 female [55.2%]). After fully adjusting for sociodemographic, lifestyle, and social factors and multiple testing, frequent cultural engagement was associated with lower risk of any mental disorders (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.62-0.82; PFDR < .001), dementia (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.56-0.89; FDR-adjusted P = .01), substance misuse (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.59-0.95; FDR-adjusted P = .04), and mood disorders (HR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.56-0.95; FDR-adjusted P = .04), but not neurotic disorders. Associations persisted after excluding early incident cases and adjusting for baseline depressive symptoms and cognition and showed robustness to unmeasured confounders. Cultural engagement was not associated with any negative control outcomes.

Conclusions and relevance: In this nationally representative cohort of older adults, cultural engagement was associated with a lower hazard of subsequent hospital-treated mental disorders, with particularly consistent associations for dementia, substance misuse, and mood disorders. These findings provide triangulated statistical data to suggest that cultural engagement is associated with reduced risk of several clinically recorded mental disorders and support further testing of cultural engagement as a population mental health strategy.

item.title: Uptake and Inequalities in Exercise-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation After Decentralization
item.description:
Importance: Despite clinical benefits and guideline recommendations, uptake of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) following coronary artery disease remains suboptimal, with barriers including transportation issues, travel distance, and geographic location. To overcome these barriers, decentralization strategies that move health care to local settings have been developed across several countries.

Objective: To determine whether CR uptake improved following decentralization, and whether geographic and social inequalities were reduced.

Design, setting, and participants: This register-based cohort study used data from 2013 to 2022, with data analysis performed from April to August 2025. This population-based study was conducted within 21 Danish municipalities. All participants were patients aged 30 years or older discharged alive after acute myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass grafting. Patients were identified in the Danish National Patient Register. Patients were excluded if they had a previous diagnosis or procedure or did not reside within the study area.

Exposures: Travel distance from home to nearest CR facility and educational level.

Main outcomes and measures: Uptake (attending at least 1 training session within 180 days from discharge) was analyzed using modified Poisson regression to quantify differences in proportions before and after decentralization with adjustment for relevant covariates.

Results: A total of 19 375 patients were eligible for the study, and 295 patients with missing information on exposures or covariates were excluded. Among the included 19 080 patients, 13 355 (70.0%) were male, and 10 868 (57.0%) were aged 60 to 79 years. The median (IQR) travel distance was reduced from 15.1 (5.9-25.7) km to 7.2 (2.8-14.8) km after decentralization, and uptake increased by 16% (risk ratio [RR], 1.16; 95% CI, 1.12-1.19). Among the 20% of patients with the longest travel distance, uptake increased by 45% (RR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.33-1.58), and geographic inequality was significantly reduced. Among patients with short education, uptake increased by 27% (RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.20-1.35), and social inequality was significantly reduced.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 19 080 patients, there was increased uptake of CR after decentralization to primary care, accompanied by significant reductions in geographic and social inequalities. The findings support decentralized delivery of CR as a feasible and equitable model, but ongoing monitoring of quality and safety remains essential.

item.title: Digital and Coaching Interventions for Uptake of Cancer Genetic Testing: The MiGHT Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Germline genetic testing (GT) for hereditary cancer risk can inform cancer treatment, screening, and prevention, yet testing rates remain low. Alternative strategies are needed to improve facilitation of GT.

Objective: To compare 2 patient-level interventions to increase uptake of hereditary cancer GT against usual care.

Design, setting, and participants: The Michigan Genetic Hereditary Testing (MiGHT) randomized clinical trial analyzed self-reported GT outcome data from participants meeting clinical GT criteria between April 21, 2022, and November 21, 2025. Participants were adults (age ≥18 years) who met national criteria for genetic evaluation and had not previously completed germline GT recruited from oncology, primary care, and gastroenterology practices; research registries; and the general public in Michigan. Data were analyzed from April 30, 2025, to May 1, 2026.

Interventions: Participants were randomized to either telephone-based health coaching, a self-directed digital intervention, or usual care. Both interventions incorporated genetics education and motivational interviewing concepts.

Main outcomes and measures: GT uptake was assessed at 6- and 12-month time points. The primary outcome was completion of GT by 6 months. The effects of study group on GT uptake were evaluated using logistic regression, adjusting for cancer history, age, gender, and race.

Results: A total of 793 participants (median [IQR] age, 64 [51-71] years; 458 [57.8%] female) were randomized to health coaching (261 participants), the digital intervention (265 participants), or usual care (267 participants). Overall, 31 participants (4.9%) reported completing GT by the 6-month time point, and 76 participants (9.6%) underwent GT across the 12-month study period. Compared with usual care, participants in the digital intervention group had higher odds of completing GT by 6 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 3.88; 97.5% CI, 1.27-14.80), while those in the health coaching group had higher odds of completing GT by 12 months (AOR, 2.25; 97.5% CI, 1.11-4.77). Participants in the digital intervention group were more likely to express intention to test at 6 months (AOR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.44-3.93), whereas those in the health coaching group had higher intention at both 6 (AOR, 2.99; 95% CI, 1.83-4.95) and 12 (AOR, 2.29; 95% CI 1.29-4.15) months compared with usual care.

Conclusions and relevance: In this randomized clinical trial of GT interventions, GT uptake was higher among participants who received the digital or health coaching interventions compared with usual care, although overall testing rates were low. These results underscore the importance of content delivery, motivational messaging, and alternative GT care models.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05162846.

item.title: Trends in Violence Against Children in Australia
item.description:
Importance: Administrative data are commonly used to monitor multiple forms of violence against children, within and external to the family, yet different systems capture distinct thresholds of harm. Reliance on single data sources may obscure population-level trends.

Objective: To examine trends in multiple indicators of children's exposure to violence in Australia from 2014 to 2024 and to assess whether trends differ across police, health, and child protection data sources.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study used a time-trend analysis of Australian national administrative data spanning from 2014 to 2024. Data sources included national police-recorded assaults, hospitalizations, and child protection data from 3 Australian national agency databases. Participants were children aged 0 to 17 years, disaggregated by sex and age group. Analyses were conducted from January to April 2026.

Exposures: Year, modeled continuously.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcomes were annual rates per 100 000 population on police-recorded sexual assault, family and domestic violence (FDV)-related assault, hospitalizations for assault, and child maltreatment substantiations. Temporal trends were modeled using quasi-Poisson regression with population offsets, and average annual percentage changes were estimated. Turning points were assessed using Davies test and segmented regression.

Results: Annual population denominators ranged from 2.6 to 2.8 million girls and 2.7 to 3.0 million boys aged 0 to 17 years. Police-recorded sexual assault rates increased steadily among girls aged 0 to 9 years (2.8% per year; 95% CI, 2.0% to 3.6% per year) and those aged 10 to 17 years (4.2% per year; 95% CI, 3.4% to 5.0% per year). Among boys aged 10 to 17 years, rates accelerated sharply after 2021 (15.7% per year; 95% CI, 5.5% to 26.9% per year). FDV-related assault showed a similar trend, with stable to modest increases before 2021 followed by steep increases thereafter. Assault-related hospitalizations were generally stable, except for declines among boys aged 10 to 17 years (-1.4% per year; 95% CI, -2.7% to -0.1% per year). Overall child maltreatment substantiation remained stable, but declines were found for physical (-3.2% per year; 95% CI, -5.2% to -1.2% year) and sexual (-3.6% per year; 95% CI, -5.2% to -2.0% per year) abuse, alongside an increase in emotional abuse substantiations to 2020 (7.6% per year; 95% CI, 5.2% to 10.0% per year), followed by a decline (-7.0% per year; 95% CI, -11.8% to -1.9% per year).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study using Australian national administrative data, trends in violence against children differed substantially across systems. Although police data indicated increased violence exposure, particularly in recent years, child-protection substantiations and hospitalizations remained stable or declined. Strengthened national surveillance is critical.

item.title: Patient Navigation Plus mHealth Incentives for Linkage to OUD Care for Adults Who Also Use Methamphetamines: A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Hospitalization is common among people with opioid use disorder (OUD) and is recognized as a reachable moment to start treatment. Methamphetamine use among people with OUD is associated with decreased linkage to postdischarge OUD care.

Objective: To determine the feasibility, acceptability, and exploratory clinical outcomes of a pilot randomized clinical trial (RCT) of an adherence-focused mobile health (mHealth) intervention aiming to increase linkage to and retention in outpatient buprenorphine services for patients hospitalized with OUD and methamphetamine use.

Design, setting, and participants: This single-site, 2-arm pilot RCT was conducted from January 3, 2024, to April 14, 2025, at a single-site, large urban safety net hospital in Seattle, Washington. Patients 18 years or older were eligible if they had initiated buprenorphine for OUD while in the hospital and had used methamphetamine within the past 30 days. Participants were randomized to the mHealth Incentivized Adherence Plus Patient Navigation (MIAPP) intervention or to treatment as usual (TAU).

Intervention: The MIAPP intervention combined financial incentives via mHealth-based adherence monitoring with a patient navigator (PN) during the first 30 days after discharge.

Main outcomes and measures: Feasibility was assessed by meeting the target enrollment of 40 participants and intervention delivery. Acceptability was measured by patient satisfaction ratings on a scale from 0 to 10, with 0 indicating not at all satisfied and 10 indicating extremely satisfied. The main pilot clinical outcome was linkage to outpatient OUD care within 30 days of hospital discharge, defined as medications for OUD being prescribed or dispensed. Other outcomes included retention in buprenorphine treatment and hospital readmissions at 90 days; past 30-day methamphetamine use was measured at the 30-day follow-up visit.

Results: The target enrollment of 40 participants (mean [SD] age, 43.4 [12.6] years) was met. Most participants (33 [82.5%]) were male. The intervention was allocated to 20 participants and delivered to 19 (95.0%); 20 participants received TAU. item.title: Federal Immigration Enforcement Deployment and Emergency Department Utilization Among Children
item.description:
Importance: Heightened immigration enforcement in the US has been associated with reduced health care utilization in immigrant communities. Pediatric emergency departments (EDs) serve as a critical safety net for children, yet the impacts of acute immigration enforcement activity in pediatric ED utilization remain incompletely characterized.

Objective: To evaluate whether deployment of federal law enforcement in Washington, DC, was associated with changes in pediatric ED utilization and whether these changes differed by the patients' preferred language, race, and ethnicity.

Design, setting, and participants: This repeated cross-sectional interrupted time series analysis compared daily pediatric ED visits from June 1 to September 30, 2025, with visits in the same calendar period in 2024 at a single pediatric ED at a freestanding children's hospital in Washington, DC. Participants included all patients younger than 26 years presenting to the pediatric ED during the study period.

Exposures: Deployment of federal law enforcement personnel, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and National Guard troops, in Washington, DC, beginning August 11, 2025.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was daily pediatric ED visit counts. Interrupted time series models estimated immediate changes in ED utilization and postdeployment trends by patient-preferred language, race, and ethnicity, adjusting for age, sex, and acuity.

Results: A total of 21 822 pediatric ED visits were included in the analysis (median age, 6.5 [IQR, 2.0-13.1] years; 11 505 visits [52.7%] by male patients). Among these visits, 6253 patients (28.7%) identified as Hispanic, 10 649 (48.8%) as non-Hispanic Black, 2200 (10.1%) as non-Hispanic White, 558 (2.6%) as non-Hispanic multiracial, 1411 (6.5%) as non-Hispanic additional race, and 652 (3.0%), unknown. Patients who preferred to speak Spanish experienced an estimated immediate change in visits following federal deployment of -10.4 visits per day, whereas patients who preferred English experienced an estimated immediate change of 5.6 visits per day (difference, -16.0 visits per day). Hispanic patients similarly experienced an estimated immediate change of -13.3 visits per day, whereas non-Hispanic patients experienced an estimated immediate change of 6.2 visits per day (difference, -19.4 visits per day). Among Hispanic patients, those preferring Spanish had greater estimated immediate changes (-12.1 visits per day) than those preferring English (-0.8 visits per day; difference, -11.3 visits per day). No significant differences were observed across non-Hispanic racial and ethnic groups. No comparable declines were observed during the same period in 2024.

Conclusion and relevance: In this repeated cross-sectional study of pediatric ED visits before and after a federal immigration enforcement deployment, heightened immigration enforcement activity was associated with an immediate reduction in pediatric ED utilization, particularly among patients who preferred to speak Spanish. item.title: Patient Experiences of Disrespectful or Judgmental Language in Medical Records
item.description:
Importance: The 21st Century Cures Act made clinical notes broadly accessible to patients. However, the frequency and patient-perceived consequences of disrespectful or judgmental language (DJL) in medical records among the general US population remain unknown.

Objectives: To (1) quantify the frequency of participant-reported DJL in medical records; (2) characterize patient-anticipated consequences; and (3) examine factors associated with DJL and documentation trust in clinicians.

Design, setting, and participants: Cross-sectional, nationally weighted survey of 500 US adults conducted from November 21 to December 4, 2025, using YouGov's nonprobability-based online panel.

Main outcomes and measures: Descriptive statistics characterized experience of DJL in medical records (patient portal users) or health care (nonportal users) and patient-anticipated consequences. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% CIs were estimated using multivariable logistic regression including sociodemographics and clinical factors for 2 outcomes: DJL and documentation trust.

Results: Among 500 respondents (mean [SE] age, 48.0 [0.9] years; 253 [51.0%] women, 53 [11.0%] Black, 80 [18.0%] Hispanic [any race], and 315 [60.0%] White, 358 portal users [71.2%]), a total of 83 participants reported DJL: 58 of 358 (17.1%) portal users in their own medical records and/or that of a loved one, and 25 of 142 nonportal users (15.6%) in health care encounters. Patient-reported consequences included 377 of 500 respondents (74.7%) who anticipated DJL would influence subsequent care from a new clinician, and 373 (73.3%) who anticipated worse health outcomes, such as wrong medication prescribing or diagnostic errors. Furthermore, 435 of 500 respondents (85.5%) anticipated they would be less likely to return to the clinician. In adjusted analyses, patients who reported low income (compared with high income: aOR, 2.64; 95% CI, 1.18-5.91; P = .03) had a greater likelihood of reporting DJL, as did those with a diagnosis of chronic pain (compared with no diagnosis of chronic pain: aOR, 3.25; 95% CI, 1.46-7.26; P = .004). The experience of DJL was associated with diminished documentation trust in clinicians (aOR, 5.76; 95% CI, 2.90-11.46; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance: In this survey study, 1 in 6 US adults reported DJL in medical records (or in health care experiences for nonportal users), disproportionately affecting those with low income or chronic pain, and DJL was associated with diminished clinician documentation trust. Patient-anticipated consequences such as diminished intent to return to clinician suggest important quality of care and system-level implications. Realizing the promise of health information transparency will require concurrent reform in respectful language in clinical documentation and health care encounters.

item.title: Out-of-Pocket Costs for Chronic Illness Management in High-Deductible Health Plans
item.description:
Importance: High-deductible health plans (HDHPs) enroll a substantial share of privately insured Americans and are associated with reduced use of care, even care that is considered medically necessary. However, the magnitude of patient out-of-pocket (OOP) costs required to obtain evidence-based medical care when enrolled in HDHPs remains poorly understood.

Objective: To estimate patient OOP costs required to receive guideline-concordant care for common chronic conditions when enrolled in an HDHP vs a non-HDHP.

Design, setting, and participants: This retrospective cohort study used 2022 to 2023 national commercial insurance claims data. Participants included adults aged 18 to 64 years with employer-sponsored insurance and previously diagnosed diabetes, hypertension, or both. To enter the cohort, persons had to have received guideline-concordant care for their chronic illnesses. Data were analyzed from July 2025 to April 2026.

Exposure: Enrollment in an HDHP vs a non-HDHP.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was annual patient OOP costs to receive evidence-based care. Entropy balancing and generalized linear models with geographic fixed effects estimated the mean OOP costs of receiving minimum recommended medical care for diabetes, hypertension, or both in HDHPs and non-HDHPs. Estimates were weighted to ensure that observed costs were representative of the full sample of chronically ill persons.

Results: There were 539 590 adults receiving guideline-concordant care who entered the cohort. After entropy balancing, groups exhibited mean covariate balance, with males representing 57.9% of HDHP enrollees and 57.8% of non-HDHP enrollees, and similar age distributions across groups, with 45.4% of both HDHP and non-HDHP enrollees 55 to 64 years of age. The estimated annual OOP cost for individuals to receive guideline-concordant diabetes care was $153.91 (95% CI, $150.18-$157.64) in HDHPs vs $68.06 (95% CI, $66.34-$69.78) in non-HDHPs; $128.94 (95% CI, $127.25-$130.64) in HDHPs vs $53.89 (95% CI, $53.20-$54.58) in non-HDHPs for guideline-concordant hypertension care; and $164.18 (95% CI, $160.93-$167.44) in HDHPs vs $100.60 (95% CI, $98.80-$102.39) in non-HDHPs for guideline-concordant care for comorbid diabetes and hypertension (all P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of a large, national sample of chronically ill adults with hypertension, diabetes, or both, annual patient costs were 1.6 to 2.4 times as high to receive recommended care in HDHPs vs non-HDHPs, although the magnitude of the difference in OOP costs was relatively small (range, $63.68 to $85.85). Findings provide novel evidence quantifying the magnitude of cost burden experienced by chronically ill patients under various insurance mechanisms and complement prior HDHP studies evaluating health care utilization.

item.title: Thrombectomy for Acute Stroke Due to Medium Vessel Occlusion Across Perfusion Mismatch Profiles: A Post Hoc Analysis of the ESCAPE-MeVO Trial
item.description:
Importance: Recent trials have not demonstrated a benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) over medical therapy in acute stroke due to medium vessel occlusion (MeVO). However, it remains uncertain whether selected patients with favorable perfusion may benefit from EVT.

Objective: To investigate the association between perfusion mismatch profiles and functional outcomes in MeVO stroke and to determine whether these profiles modify the effect of EVT.

Design, setting, and participants: This study was a post hoc analysis of ESCAPE-MeVO (Endovascular Treatment to Improve Outcomes for Medium Vessel Occlusion), a multicenter randomized clinical trial conducted in North America, Europe, and the United Kingdom between April 2022 and June 2024, with a 90-day follow-up. Trial participants included patients with acute MeVO stroke presenting within 12 hours from last known well and evidence of salvageable brain tissue. This analysis included only patients with interpretable baseline perfusion imaging. Data were analyzed from March to July 2026.

Interventions: Randomization to EVT plus usual care vs usual care alone.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score. Secondary outcomes included 24-hour follow-up infarct volume and 90-day mRS score of 0 to 1 and 0 to 2. Perfusion mismatch ratio and volume were defined as the ratio and difference between the critically hypoperfused area and the ischemic core, with volume thresholds defined by site-specific postprocessing software.

Results: Of 530 enrolled patients, 309 (58.3%) had available baseline perfusion imaging and were included in this study (EVT: n = 146; usual care: n = 163). Patient median (IQR) age was 73 (63-82) years, and 141 (45.6%) were women. Median (IQR) perfusion mismatch volume was 37.2 (22.1-57.2) mL, and the median (IQR) mismatch ratio was 6.1 (2.8-10.0). Ordinal 90-day mRS score was not associated with perfusion mismatch volume (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.03 [95% CI, 0.99-1.07] per 10-mL increase) or perfusion mismatch ratio (AOR, 1.03 [95% CI, 0.97-1.09] per 1-unit increase). There was no modification of EVT effect by perfusion mismatch volume or ratio on ordinal 90-day mRS. Results were consistent across secondary outcomes and subgroups.

Conclusions and relevance: In this exploratory post hoc analysis of acute MeVO stroke, perfusion mismatch profiles were not associated with functional outcomes and did not modify the effect of EVT. These findings suggest that perfusion imaging profiles based on currently used thresholds and cutoffs did not identify patients likely to benefit from EVT in the ESCAPE-MeVO trial.

item.title: Home-Based Programs and Cardiac Rehabilitation Participation Among Veterans With Ischemic Heart Disease
item.description:
Importance: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a guideline-recommended secondary prevention program that reduces morbidity and mortality among patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD) yet remains underutilized. Over the past decade, the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) has implemented strategies to increase CR participation, including expansion of virtual home-based CR (HBCR) programs as alternatives to traditional center-based CR (CBCR).

Objective: To examine temporal trends and factors associated with CR participation among veterans with IHD.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study used national VHA electronic health record data to evaluate CR participation among veterans hospitalized for IHD, identified using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9), ICD-10, or Current Procedural Terminology codes from 2012 to 2022. Data were analyzed from October 25, 2025, to July 25, 2026.

Exposures: Availability of CR delivery models at Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities, including referral to community care programs only, VA CBCR, or VA HBCR.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the proportion of eligible veterans with acute myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass graft surgery who participated in any type of CR within 12 months of the index event, identified using Current Procedural Terminology codes and VA stop codes from VA-provided, VA-purchased, or Medicare-claimed services. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with CR participation.

Results: Among 405 907 veterans with IHD (mean [SD] age, 68.5 [11.1] years; 391 998 men [96.6%]), 63 185 (15.6%) participated in CR. Participation increased from 9.6% in 2012 to 17.1% in 2022, with a peak of 19.7% in 2018. In 2022, participation was higher at facilities offering HBCR (20.0%) compared with those offering CBCR without HBCR (14.8%) or referral to community care programs only (14.3%). The adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of participation among veterans treated at facilities offering HBCR was 1.80 (95% CI, 1.75-1.84), whereas the AOR of participation at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR was 1.29 (95% CI, 1.26-1.32) compared with referral to community care programs only.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of veterans with IHD, participation in CR nearly doubled between 2012 and 2022. Patients who had index events at facilities offering HBCR had higher CR participation than those at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR, or at facilities offering only referral to community care. Broader availability of HBCR programs may help improve participation within large health systems.

item.title: Maternal Prenatal Diet and Colic and Eczema Among Infants
item.description:
Importance: Infantile colic is a disorder of gut-brain interaction whose cause is poorly understood.

Objective: To estimate associations of maternal diet quality and intakes of specific allergenic foods with infant eczema and colic.

Design, setting, and participants: Project Viva prospective cohort of 2128 mother-child pairs unselected for atopic risk with recruitment in early pregnancy in Eastern Massachusetts from April 1999 to November 2002, with follow-up to October 2003, and data analysis November 2025 to July 2026.

Exposures: Prenatal diet via food frequency questionnaires in early pregnancy (median [IQR], 9.9 [8.8-11.3] weeks) and midpregnancy (median [IQR], 27.9 [26.7-28.8] weeks). The Mediterranean Diet Score (MDS) and Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) were calculated and intake of commonly allergenic foods was determined.

Main outcomes and measures: Maternal report of colic symptoms and eczema diagnosis at median (IQR) of 6.3 (6.0-6.8) months.

Results: Among 1324 pairs with exposure and outcome data, mean (SD) maternal age was 32.6 (4.6) years, 667 (50.4%) were nulliparous, and 532 (40.2%) reported a history of atopy; 152 (11.5%) infants had eczema alone, 273 (20.6%) had colic alone, and 61 (4.6%) had both. In multinomial logistic regression models adjusted for maternal age, race, ethnicity, education, parity, smoking, and atopy, greater mean (SD) MDS (4.6 [2.0] points) was associated with lower odds of colic and eczema (odds ratio [OR], 0.85; 95% CI, 0.74-0.98 per 1 point), and mean (SD) DII (-2.7 [1.3]) was associated with higher odds (OR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.12-1.61 per 1 point). Neither diet score was associated with eczema or colic alone. Seafood intake was associated with lower odds of colic and eczema combined (OR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.58-0.97 per weekly serving). Nut intake was associated with higher risk for colic among those without eczema (eg, OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.09 per weekly serving of any nuts or peanuts), but not with colic and eczema combined (OR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.88-1.07). Dairy or egg intakes were not associated with any outcomes. Associations of dietary scores and fish intake with colic were stronger among infants of atopic mothers.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 1324 mother-child pairs, poorer maternal diet quality and lower seafood intake were associated with infantile colic with eczema or maternal atopic history.
